title: refactor: move the find-the-verse win card onto Dialog
summary: When you win a Find the Verse round, the "You found it!" card now uses the app's shared pop-up window. The card looks a little different, the keyboard can no longer wander off it to the page behind, and screen readers announce it as a window that needs an answer. One thing works differently on purpose: tapping the Bible text outside the card now closes the card (like **Keep reading**) instead of reaching the reader with the card still up.

links.label: PR 2200: the shared Dialog this card now uses

setup.title: Open the preview build
setup.body: Use the **Open the preview build** button above, in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox on a computer (one test later uses a phone). If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload.

setup.title: Make sure you're seeing the new version
setup.body: The app saves a copy of itself in your browser. If anything looks like an older version, do a hard refresh: Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, or Cmd+Shift+R on Mac.

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Games are saved to your account. Open **Settings** (the gear icon), choose to sign in, enter your email address, then type the code that arrives in your inbox. Use an inbox you can check.

setup.title: Install the Find the Verse extension
setup.body: Open **Settings** › **Extensions**. If **Find the Verse** isn't already installed, open it and choose **Install**. If you can't find **Find the Verse** at all, mark every test **Blocked** and say so in the note.

setup.title: Make a quick game to win
setup.body: Open **Find the Verse** from the toolbar (the crosshair / target icon, or the **...** menu) and choose **Create a game**. Give it any name, pick an easy secret verse (type `John 1:1` and choose **Go**), fill in the hints, and save it. You'll play this game several times: from the game list, start it, then tap verses in John 1 until you tap verse 1. That shows the win card. "The bar" below means the small game bar that shows over the reader during a round.

tests.title: Winning shows confetti and the card, with the reader still bright behind it
steps: Start your game from the game list and tap verses until you tap the secret verse.
Look at the screen as the win appears.
expected: Confetti falls over the Bible text, and a card appears in the middle of the screen with 🎉, **You found it!**, the verse reference and its text, and how many guesses you took.
The confetti falls behind the card, not over it.
The Bible text behind the card is **not** darkened or greyed out.
The card has two buttons, **Back to games** and **Keep reading**, and a sound toggle below them. There is no ✕ close button in the corner.
The text in the card is centered, and the card is no wider than about a phone's width.

tests.title: The keyboard starts on Back to games and stays inside the card
steps: Win a round again.
Without clicking anything, look for the keyboard focus ring (press Tab once and then Shift+Tab if you don't see one).
Press Tab several times, more times than there are buttons on the card.
expected: When the card appears, **Back to games** is the button with the keyboard focus ring.
Tab moves between **Back to games**, **Keep reading** and the sound toggle, then goes back around to **Back to games**.
Focus never moves to the reader, the toolbar or anything else behind the card.

tests.title: Escape closes the card and keeps the round's bar
steps: Win a round again.
Press Escape.
expected: The card and confetti go away.
You stay on the Bible text, and the game bar still shows, saying **You found it!**.
You can scroll and tap verses in the reader again straight away.

tests.title: Tapping the Bible text outside the card closes it
tests.why: This is the one intended behavior change: before, a tap outside reached the reader while the card stayed up. Now it closes the card first, the same as **Keep reading**.
steps: Win a round again.
Click (or tap) a verse in the Bible text away from the card.
Then click a verse in the reader once more.
expected: The first click closes the card and the confetti. The game bar still shows **You found it!**.
The first click does **not** also do something in the reader (it doesn't select that verse or count as a guess).
The second click works normally in the reader.

tests.title: Keep reading closes the card
steps: Win a round again.
Choose **Keep reading**.
expected: The card and confetti go away and the game bar still shows **You found it!**, the same as Escape.

tests.title: Back to games returns to the game list
steps: Win a round again.
Choose **Back to games** (or press Enter right away, since it starts with the focus).
expected: The card closes and the Find the Verse panel shows your game list.

tests.title: The sound toggle still works on the card
tests.before: Turn your computer's volume up a little.
steps: Win a round. Note whether you hear the victory sound.
On the card, use the sound toggle, and watch its label.
Win again.
expected: The toggle switches between **Victory sound on** and **Victory sound off**, and the card stays open when you use it.
The next win plays the sound only if the toggle is on.

sections.title: Phone, dark mode and screen readers

tests.title: The card fits a phone screen
steps: Open the preview on a phone (or make your browser window narrow, about the width of a phone).
Sign in, start your game and win a round.
Tap the Bible text outside the card.
expected: The whole card fits on screen with a little space at each side. No text or button is cut off, and the page doesn't scroll sideways.
Confetti falls over the reader behind the card.
Tapping outside the card closes it and the game bar shows **You found it!**.

tests.title: The card is readable in dark mode
steps: In **Settings**, switch to dark mode.
Win a round.
expected: The card has a dark background with light text, matching the app's other pop-up windows. Every line and button is easy to read.

tests.title: A screen reader announces the card as a window
tests.before: Optional: skip this test if you don't use a screen reader. On Mac, VoiceOver turns on with Cmd+F5; on Windows, Narrator turns on with Ctrl+Windows+Enter.
steps: Turn on your screen reader.
Win a round and listen to what's read out.
expected: It says you're in a dialog (or window) called **You found it!**, then reads **Back to games**.
Moving through the card with the screen reader stays inside the card.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: The rest of the game still works after a win
steps: After closing a win card with **Keep reading**, use the game bar's buttons (for example go back to the game list from it).
Start the game again and play a round to the win.
expected: The bar's buttons work as before.
A new round starts and can be won again, showing the card again.

tests.title: Other pop-up windows still open and close
tests.why: The win card now shares its pop-up window with other parts of the app, so check one of them still behaves.
steps: Sign out, then choose to sign in again (from **Settings**) so the sign-in window opens.
Press Escape.
expected: The sign-in window opens, dims the page behind it as before, and closes with Escape.

notCovered: With your system's "reduce motion" setting on, the confetti should not show. This was already the case before the change and is hard to set up for most testers.
The automated tests for the win card (that it's a dialog, where the focus starts, and that Escape keeps reading) run on their own and don't need checking by hand.
